since a length difference of d means one pointer would otherwise start d steps ahead, swapping onto the other list at the end automatically cancels out that offset, so the pointers land on the intersection node at the same step (or both reach null/end together if there's no intersection)
commonMistakes: comparing node values instead of node identity, which gives false positives when two different nodes happen to share a value
forgetting to redirect a pointer to the other list's head once it reaches the end, causing an infinite loop or a null result
not handling the no-intersection case, where both pointers should end up at the end together

content.problemStatement:
You're given two singly linked lists as arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, each
holding node values in order. The two lists may share a common tail: a
suffix of `nums1` starting at index `skipA` is the exact same run of
nodes as the suffix of `nums2` starting at index `skipB` (same values,
same length, representing one physically shared chain of nodes).
`skipA` and `skipB` are given directly and tell you where that shared
tail begins in each array (0-indexed).

**Return the value at the intersection node (the first node of the
shared tail), or -1 if there is no intersection.**

If the lists do not intersect at all, `skipA` and `skipB` are both -1
and should be ignored.
constraints: either both skipA and skipB are -1 (no intersection), or both are valid 0-indexed positions marking the start of an identical, equal-length suffix in each array
notes: the lists intersect at their very first node (entirely shared)
the intersection point is near the end of both lists
